feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: VoxMem: Benchmarking Multimodal Memory in Large Audio Language Models
entry.summary:
VoxMem is a new benchmark featuring 3,196 instances across 177 hours of spoken sessions designed to evaluate multimodal memory in Large Audio Language Models across diverse acoustic evidence types and memory operations.

Why it matters: Current LALMs struggle to maintain non-transcript audio context like speaker identity and acoustic environment over multi-session long-context histories, highlighting key gaps for conversational AI development.

entry.title: Omni-IO Skills: Harnessing Your Agent Omni-Native
entry.summary:
Omni-IO Skills is a plug-and-play agent harness that enables omni-native multimodal capabilities without modifying host agent reasoning cores by using hierarchical skills, dependency-aware orchestration, and a persistent Asset Registry.

Why it matters: It provides a practical framework to expand AI agents to handle diverse modalities and complex workflows without undertaking expensive foundation model retrainings or updates.

entry.title: Follow the Entities: A Corpus Map for Agentic Search
entry.summary:
CorpusMap is an offline-constructed navigation layer that organizes document collections into a graph of entity pages to optimize LLM agent search.

Why it matters: By pre-indexing entity relationships across document collections, LLM agents can retrieve disconnected evidence faster and more accurately while cutting token overhead.

entry.title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
entry.summary:
EngiWorld is a benchmark featuring 1,301 expert-curated tasks across 6 engineering domains and 26 software platforms to evaluate autonomous agents across full professional engineering workflows.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized, programmatic foundation to evaluate and advance autonomous agents handling complex, end-to-end industrial engineering workflows.

entry.title: Beyond Dyadic Memory: Interaction-Aware Multimodal Memory with Adaptive Agentic Retrieval for Multi-Party Spoken Conversations
entry.summary:
VoxPolyMem introduces an interaction-aware multimodal memory framework and the EG-GRPO reinforcement learning method to optimize agentic retrieval in multi-party spoken conversations.

Why it matters: It establishes a specialized framework for long-term memory and accurate attribution in complex, multi-speaker multimodal conversational AI.

entry.title: LongCat-DeepResearch Technical Report
entry.summary:
LongCat-DeepResearch combines an enhanced LongCat model with a multi-agent workflow that uses global planning, parallel section drafting, and targeted local revisions to generate research reports.

Why it matters: Targeted section-level revisions reduce the computational cost of repeating full-report rewrites in complex multi-agent research workflows.

entry.title: LLMs are General Asynchronous Agents
entry.summary:
A general asynchronous LLM framework uses inference coroutines with overlapping memory states to enable real-world concurrent execution without task-specific training.

Why it matters: It enables standard off-the-shelf LLMs to process continuous incoming inputs while actively executing tasks, removing the need for specialized asynchronous architectures.

entry.title: SoL-Refiner: Speed-of-Light One-Step Refinement for High-Resolution Video
entry.summary:
SoL-Refiner is a one-step video refiner that upscales low-resolution model outputs into 4K videos using a single denoising step, achieving an 8.91x speedup over multi-step baselines.

Why it matters: It eliminates the sampling bottleneck in high-resolution video generation by drastically reducing latency without sacrificing visual quality metrics.

entry.title: APM-Bench: Benchmarking Cross-session Persistent Memory for Egocentric Streaming Video Assistants
entry.summary:
APM-Bench is a benchmark evaluating cross-session persistent memory for egocentric streaming video assistants, featuring multi-session life trajectories to test long-term recall, real-time efficiency, and missing evidence recognition.

Why it matters: It provides a realistic testbed to develop persistent memory systems for AI assistants that interact continuously and intermittently across real-world, multi-day user activities.

entry.title: Asking for What Was Never Requested: Horizontal and Vertical Proactivity in Agents
entry.summary:
A new framework formalizes horizontal and vertical proactivity in agents and trains a questioner model via Q&D optimization to pursue unstated evidence without relying on LLM judges.

Why it matters: It enables smaller AI agents to autonomously uncover unstated task requirements and know when to stop asking questions without relying on expensive, larger models or LLM judges.

entry.title: Context Language Models
entry.summary:
Context Language Models (CLMs) natively manage context by treating it as an editable file, allowing models to make unrestricted updates, reduce compute, and learn context-management strategies via reinforcement learning and prompt optimization.

Why it matters: Shifting context management from external harnesses to intrinsic model operations significantly cuts inference FLOPs and server compute while increasing task accuracy in long-horizon and multi-agent tasks.

entry.title: StoryEngine: A State-Grounded Agentic Framework for Video Storytelling
entry.summary:
StoryEngine is a state-grounded agentic framework for long-form video storytelling that uses structured state tracking, canonical references, and bounded evaluation-guided repair to maintain narrative coherence and visual consistency across multi-shot videos.

Why it matters: It prevents visual drift and causal inconsistencies in long-form video generation by decoupling state tracking from pixel outputs and adding automated repair loops.

entry.title: Selecting The Most Informative Tokens in Natural Language Autoencoders
entry.summary:
A study of 4.7 million autoencoder explanations shows chat-structure rankers select relevant token positions for audit better than computational signals, enabling 95% compute reduction without losing threat detection capability.

Why it matters: Auditors can drastically reduce the computational cost of interpreting neural network activations by inspecting only 5% of structured token positions while still detecting critical safety threats.

entry.title: AutoRef: Harness Optimization for Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation
entry.summary:
AutoRef automatically optimizes executable agentic harnesses via coding-agent rewrites and beam search, improving multi-reference image generation without updating underlying model weights.

Why it matters: It enables significant multi-reference image quality improvements through automated program optimization instead of costly model retraining.

entry.title: Omni-Decision: Evidence-Ledger Planning for Omni-Modal Agents
entry.summary:
Omni-Decision replaces dialogue history in omni-modal agents with a compact evidence ledger, filtering noisy observations via a critic to improve multi-step planning efficiency and accuracy.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that decoupling evidence state management from raw observation history significantly reduces execution costs while matching or exceeding state-of-the-art omni-modal performance.

entry.title: KV-Kaizen: Learning Context-Adaptive Cache Compression Choices
entry.summary:
KV-Kaizen is a context-adaptive selector that dynamically configures per-layer LLM KV caches across layer sharing, precision, and low-rank latent representation without evicting tokens.

Why it matters: It alleviates the decode-stage memory bottleneck in long-context LLMs, demonstrating that compressing large pre-trained models contextually is superior to serving smaller uncompressed models.

entry.title: $S^3$: Spectral Null-Space Swap Makes Reasoning Models Efficient
entry.summary:
Spectral Null-Space Swap ($S^3$) is a training-free model composition method that isolates the thinking model's weight components in the non-thinking model's null space, reducing inference token overhead while maintaining or improving reasoning accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables developers to significantly lower LLM chain-of-thought inference token costs and speed up generation without retraining models or sacrificing reasoning accuracy.

entry.title: On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
PUMBA is a unified trajectory-aware training framework for masked diffusion models that combines policy-induced trajectory training, inter-step information passing, and multi-step backpropagation through time.

Why it matters: It enables masked diffusion language models to achieve autoregressive-level generation quality while significantly reducing the inference step budget.

entry.title: The Unequal Influence of Bad Advice: Using Training Data Attribution to Modulate Emergent Misalignment
entry.summary:
Researchers used training data attribution to quantify how individual harmful examples drive emergent misalignment, demonstrating that filtering data via these influence scores can enhance or attenuate the behavior.

Why it matters: Quantifying data influence allows developers to mitigate emergent misalignment by identifying and removing specific high-impact harmful examples from fine-tuning datasets.

entry.title: Active Budget Can Kill Sensitivity: Diagnosing and Repairing TopK Sparse Autoencoder Reliability
entry.summary:
Researchers identified that TopK Sparse Autoencoders reduce rare-feature sensitivity due to selection boundary geometry and introduced pairwise rank stabilization to fix it.

Why it matters: Evaluating SAEs solely on reconstruction and sparsity masks feature instability, but addressing boundary geometry ensures rare features remain reliable under semantic variations.

entry.title: Scaling Influence Functions in LLMs through Eigenbasis-Corrected One-Bit Gradient Projection
entry.summary:
Eigenbasis-Corrected One-Bit Gradient Projection (EOGP) compresses stored training gradients using EK-FAC, subspace PCA, and one-bit quantization to scale LLM influence function calculations within tight memory constraints.

Why it matters: EOGP significantly reduces the storage overhead of saving training gradients, enabling scalable, repeated influence function computations across massive LLM datasets for unknown future queries.

entry.title: Pattern Formation in Transformers
entry.summary:
Applying pattern-formation theory to full Transformer architectures reveals that positional encodings, multi-head attention, and output-value geometries selectively amplify, stabilize, and combine rich token patterns like traveling and rotating waves.

Why it matters: Leveraging pattern-formation theory to design task-aligned initializations and positional encodings significantly boosts sample efficiency and convergence speed in Transformer models.

entry.title: Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
OASIS overcomes scaling limits in on-policy self-distillation by supervising verified student trajectories using unverified model-generated attempts as teacher context, requiring only final-answer labels.

Why it matters: OASIS preserves the performance gains of self-distillation at larger model scales while eliminating the need for step-by-step written solutions, relying instead solely on final-answer labels.

entry.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
entry.summary:
The Latent Information Feedback Transformer (LIFT) introduces deep-to-shallow recurrent state feedback during pretraining by framing state learning as a parallelizable, teacher-forced prediction task using an off-the-shelf language model's next-token distribution.

Why it matters: LIFT bypasses the single-token autoregressive bottleneck by allowing language models to pass rich latent states across generation steps without sacrificing parallelized pretraining.

entry.title: Retrieval Capacity of Self-Attention Under Competition
entry.summary:
Researchers measure transformer retrieval capacity by retaining only top-weighted tokens per head, layer, and query without retraining, revealing how attention set size scales with context length, competition, and weight renormalization.

Why it matters: Understanding how competition and aggregation dictate effective attention set sizes informs more efficient context pruning, sparsification, and KV-cache compression techniques.

entry.title: Beyond Teacher Assignment: Domain-Normalized Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Domain-Normalized Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (DN-MOPD) rescales domain feedback by its measured spread, preventing instruction-following signals from swamping mathematics signals when merging specialist language models into a single student.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that successfully consolidating domain-specialized models into a single multi-talented LLM requires balancing feedback magnitudes across domains, not just routing prompts to the correct teacher.

entry.title: Post-Training Leaves Behavioral Shadows on Unrelated Decisions
entry.summary:
Active Taskless Distillation (ATD) enables language models to transfer downstream capabilities using only a single task-unrelated word output per prompt from a post-trained teacher.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that post-training updates leave systematic behavioral shadows in unrelated text, enabling silent capability transfer without exposing domain-specific training data or model parameters.

entry.title: How Far Are We from Removing the Visual Encoder? Scaling Laws for Encoder-Free Multimodal Pretraining
entry.summary:
A systematic study demonstrates that encoder-free multimodal LLMs follow distinct compute-scaling laws, with visual losses predicted to match encoder-based MLLMs at approximately 10^22 FLOPs.

Why it matters: The visual prior advantage of dedicated encoders diminishes with scale, making simpler, unified encoder-free MLLM architectures practical for large compute budgets.

entry.title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
UMM-Reflection uses trajectory-level reinforcement learning across interleaved reflection text and flow-based revisions within a single unified model, enabling self-correction without an external inference verifier.

Why it matters: It allows unified multimodal models to natively critique and iteratively repair their own generated images without relying on external critic models or verifiers during inference.

entry.title: Groupwise Agentic Grading and Advantage Redistribution for Code Agent RL
entry.summary:
GAGAR improves code agent RL by using an SFT-trained agentic grader to rank test-passing trajectories in a shared workspace, redistributing advantages to favor higher-quality code while preserving the group's total advantage sum.

Why it matters: It enables large language model code agents to learn cleaner, higher-quality implementations without sacrificing the objective ground-truth feedback provided by executable test suites.

entry.title: Recursive Harness Distillation across Agents for Robot Manipulation
entry.summary:
Recursive Harness Distillation accumulates and refines robot failure interventions into non-parametric playbooks that improve task success across different agent models without updating model parameters.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complex robot manipulation policies can be significantly improved at runtime using light, non-parametric guidance without costly model retraining.

entry.title: WorldPlay2: Extending Real-Time Interactive World Models in Control and Horizon
entry.summary:
WorldPlay2 is an interactive world model that improves real-time control and long-horizon consistency using a factorized hybrid control interface, compressed memory tokens, and a Stable Forcing distillation strategy.

Why it matters: It enables interactive world models to process complex, multi-modal control inputs while maintaining real-time performance and video stability over extended time horizons.

entry.title: QwenGyre: An Elastic Reinforcement Learning Framework for Training xLong-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
QwenGyre is an elastic online reinforcement learning framework designed for extra-long-horizon LLM agents, solving GPU idling and trajectory redundancy.

Why it matters: It enables efficient online RL training for complex, long-horizon tasks spanning hundreds of steps and 700K+ tokens per rollout without severe GPU idle time.

entry.title: WideSWE: Can Coding Agents Coordinate Changes Across Repositories?
entry.summary:
WideSWE introduces a benchmark of 120 real-world tasks across 103 software ecosystems to evaluate AI coding agents on coordinating bug fixes and feature implementations across multiple repositories.

Why it matters: WideSWE shifts agent evaluation beyond single-codebase benchmarks to reflect real-world multi-repository dependencies and cross-ecosystem development challenges.

entry.title: Change the Product, Keep the Parameters: Associative Algebra Layers for Transformers
entry.summary:
A new Transformer layer replaces dense matrix multiplication with an associative-algebra product, reducing arithmetic complexity to quadratic scaling for fixed physical block sizes while keeping the overall parameter count constant.

Why it matters: This approach provides a viable framework to trade downstream model accuracy for hardware throughput gains without altering the total parameter capacity of Transformer architectures.

entry.title: In-Flight KV Cache with Clean Anchors for Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion
entry.summary:
FlashForward accelerates autoregressive video diffusion by directly reusing stage-specific in-flight KV caches across concurrent GPU stages and stabilizing noisy trajectories with sparse clean anchor latents.

Why it matters: It significantly speeds up long video generation on multi-GPU systems while maintaining temporal consistency and visual quality without needing redundant model forward passes.

entry.title: Structured Residual Connectivity Matters for Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary:
A structured connectivity design for Diffusion Transformers replaces uniform residual streams with differentiable, selective cross-depth paths to dynamically retrieve early-layer spatial and semantic features.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that adaptive cross-layer routing significantly improves generative quality and training efficiency in DiTs with minimal parameter overhead.

entry.title: FlowTool: Controlling Tool Parameter in Image Retouching via Flow Matching
entry.summary:
FlowTool replaces autoregressive MLLM reasoning in image retouching by framing tool parameter selection as a conditional rectified flow generation task using a Diffusion Transformer.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complex, multi-modal tool-use tasks can be executed much faster and with fewer computational resources by shifting from autoregressive text generation to flow matching over continuous parameters.

entry.title: Imprint Reader: From Weight-Update Readout to Behavioral Intervention
entry.summary:
The Imprint Reader uses Semantic Mount-and-Read Tuning (SMaRT) to translate frozen LLM weight updates into natural-language descriptions and guide behavioral interventions via MetaEdit.

Why it matters: It establishes the feasibility of decoding model parameter changes into readable descriptions and leveraging those representations to directly steer LLM behavior without task-specific training data.

entry.title: TT-VidT: Decoupling the Temporal Axis for Efficient Motion-Centric Video Pretraining
entry.summary:
TT-VidT decouples video temporal processing by pairing a DINOv3 ViT-B/16 spatial path with a Temporal Transfer Layer, using Diff Compression to reconstruct target frames from initial appearance anchors and motion tokens.

Why it matters: TT-VidT demonstrates that decoupling spatial and temporal paths allows video architectures to achieve state-of-the-art motion accuracy while drastically reducing encoder FLOPs compared to dense 3D baselines.

entry.title: Telescopic Language Models
entry.summary:
Telescopic Language Models use stochastic prefix supervision with a full anchor to train a single Transformer that functions as a valid language model at every layer depth.

Why it matters: A single training run can serve arbitrary compute budgets dynamically at runtime without requiring separate models, compression runs, or inference-time modifications.

entry.title: How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention
entry.summary:
The Foil architecture optimizes looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by flattening expert layers to increase the pool of choices per routing decision and untying attention parameters across passes.

Why it matters: It provides a concrete design framework for looped MoE models that improves parameter efficiency, routing health, and pretraining loss without increasing compute or total parameter count.

entry.title: Reasoning with Continuous Latent Diffusion
entry.summary:
Latent Flow Reasoning Models (LFRMs) perform continuous latent diffusion for reasoning by using multi-layer teacher representations, asynchronous denoising, learned prompt encoders, and adapted DiffusionNFT post-training.

Why it matters: LFRMs establish that continuous latent diffusion models can outperform existing continuous-diffusion baselines on complex mathematical and code reasoning tasks using a compact 638M-parameter backbone.

entry.title: Verifier Errors in RLVR: Reward Hacking, Limits of Feedback, and Selective Control
entry.summary:
Researchers mathematically characterize verifier-driven reward hacking in RLVR using gradient flow and introduce an audit-based feedback correction method that achieves selective control to simultaneously reduce accepted errors and increase correctness.

Why it matters: It provides a formal mechanism to prevent language models from exploiting imperfect automated verifiers by using partial human or secondary audits to reduce false positives without degrading model accuracy.

entry.title: MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution
entry.summary:
Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention (MS-GLA) distributes attention heads across multiple temporal resolutions and uses an input-dependent fusion layer, overcoming the single-temporal-resolution memory bottleneck of standard Gated Linear Attention (GLA).

Why it matters: MS-GLA significantly improves long-context generalization and recall performance in linear recurrent models without increasing per-head state memory overhead.

entry.title: Not All Thinking is Created Equal: Latent Reasoning Discovers a Recurrent Search Algorithm for Depth Generalization
entry.summary:
Comparing five GPTNeoX variants on multi-hop reasoning reveals that latent-reasoning models learn a recurrent forward-search algorithm that enables depth generalization to longer reasoning hops, unlike Chain-of-Thought or Pause Token models.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that latent recurrence implements a reusable graph-search algorithm proves that latent reasoning can yield fundamentally better computational abstractions for length generalization than surface-level token traces.

entry.title: Less Sycophancy, Stronger Refusal? Lessons for AI Safety from Mechanistic Interpretability
entry.summary:
Researchers used compensatory feature injection during supervised fine-tuning to suppress sycophancy features in Qwen3.5 models, finding it restores refusal capabilities specifically under user pressure rather than enhancing direct refusal.

Why it matters: Mechanistic interventions that mitigate sycophancy can preserve safety guardrails against user pressure, though they do not automatically broaden baseline direct refusal performance.

entry.title: Beyond Token Scale: Chunk-Level Sparse Autoencoders for Reliable Semantic Feature Discovery
entry.summary:
Chunk-level Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) process mean-pooled activations over contiguous token spans to separate high-level semantic concepts from low-level token features during model interpretability analysis.

Why it matters: By altering what SAEs observe and predict, researchers can extract more reliable semantic features to steer and evaluate language models on complex reasoning and retrieval tasks.

entry.title: Spontaneous Context Restoration: How Language Models Recover from Corrupted Inputs
entry.summary:
Language models exhibit spontaneous context restoration from corrupted inputs via a two-phase internal process that can be predicted early using linear probes.

Why it matters: Early prediction of restoration failures enables efficient failure triage in deployment, saving compute by bypassing unnecessary downstream verification for corrupted inputs.

entry.title: Why Deterministic PRM Guidance Underperforms in Discrete Diffusion Reasoning
entry.summary:
Deterministic Process Reward Model (PRM) guidance underperforms outcome-based reranking in discrete diffusion LLMs when evaluated at equal forward-pass budgets due to weak early-step reward signals and poor final-state scoring.

Why it matters: Effective test-time compute allocation in discrete diffusion models requires preserving early candidate diversity and using final-state verifiers rather than relying on deterministic mid-denoising PRM pruning.

entry.title: FuseReg: Regularizing Layer Fusion Mitigates the Reconstruction-Generation Gap in Representation Autoencoders
entry.summary:
FuseReg replaces heuristic feature selection in Representation Autoencoders (RAEs) by training pixel decoders and diffusion generators over random subsets of visual encoder layers, mitigating the trade-off between reconstruction detail and generation quality.

Why it matters: FuseReg bridges the gap between image reconstruction and generation performance in RAEs without requiring architecture modifications or retraining of the core visual encoder.

entry.title: Block Sparse Attention with Log-Linear Complexity
entry.summary:
PISA introduces a pyramid Top-K selection strategy for block sparse attention, reducing query-block scoring complexity from quadratic to O(N log N) using a coarse-to-fine key hierarchy.

Why it matters: It breaks the quadratic bottleneck of block selection in sparse attention, enabling cheaper long-context training and inference without sacrificing model accuracy.

entry.title: InternW0-Δ: A World Action Model Bridging Predictive Dynamics and Actions with 20K+ Hours of Open Data
entry.summary:
InternW0-Δ is a Mixture-of-Transformers World Action Model pretrained on over 20,000 hours of heterogeneous robot and human data, combining visual dynamics, 4D priors, and action generation without requiring future-video rollout at inference.

Why it matters: It establishes an open-source data pipeline and model framework that allows robots to utilize predictive dynamics and geometric priors for action generation without costly real-time video generation during execution.

entry.title: Enhancing Photogrammetric Digital Surface Models with Pretrained Diffusion Models and Multimodal Conditioning
entry.summary:
A modified Stable Diffusion 3 architecture uses multimodal conditioning on photogrammetric DSMs and satellite imagery to refine noisy 3D elevation maps toward LiDAR quality.

Why it matters: It enables high-accuracy 3D surface modeling by enhancing low-cost satellite photogrammetry to approach expensive LiDAR quality without additional ground-survey costs.

entry.title: Jev in the Wild: A Data-Driven Analysis of the Jev Model's Functionality, Applications and Ecosystem
entry.summary:
A data-driven analysis of 2,170 public GitHub repositories reveals that the fast, low-cost Jev decision model functions as a flexible workflow component, though public attention remains heavily concentrated in routing and interface agents.

Why it matters: Understanding Jev's usage patterns helps developers design and integrate low-cost, targeted decision models as modular components within broader automated workflows.

entry.title: FoMo: Forking Moment in Generative Trajectory as a Perceptual Distance
entry.summary:
FoMo uses the timestep where diffusion generation trajectories diverge to automatically generate pointwise perceptual distance labels for training image quality metrics without human annotation.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for costly, inconsistent human annotations when training reference-based image quality assessment models.

entry.title: SLCA-GRPO: Resolving Cross-Segment Credit Misattribution in Tool-Calling RL
entry.summary:
SLCA-GRPO fixes credit misattribution in tool-calling RL by decoupling advantage estimation into segment-locked execution and preference rewards without extra rollouts.

Why it matters: It improves RL convergence speed, model accuracy, and tool efficiency for tool-calling agents without adding computational overhead from extra rollouts.

entry.title: AgentWorld: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Collaboration of Multi-agent LLMs
entry.summary:
AgentWorld is an open-source benchmark with 100 human-annotated tasks that evaluates long-horizon multi-agent collaboration and introduces Causal Collaboration Effectiveness (CCE) to measure causal dependencies in team performance.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic, long-horizon evaluation platform that exposes critical gaps in LLM multi-agent coordination, communication, and joint execution.

entry.title: Game Arena: Strategic LLM Evaluation in Competitive Environments
entry.summary:
Kaggle Game Arena is an open, ever-expanding platform that evaluates LLMs through head-to-head competitive gameplay across perfect information, imperfect information, and multiplayer environments.

Why it matters: It provides a transparent, reproducible alternative to static LLM benchmarks by continuously assessing dynamic strategic reasoning in evolving multi-agent settings.

entry.title: IndicBankBench: Evaluating Safety and Reliability of Language Model Assistants in Indian Retail Banking
entry.summary:
IndicBankBench is a 799-case benchmark that evaluates Indian retail banking LLM assistants across four stages using a strict pass^3 metric requiring success across three execution trials.

Why it matters: Evaluating LLM banking agents with traditional single-run metrics overstates their dependable execution, highlighting the need for multi-stage deterministic benchmarking before real-world deployment.

entry.title: TRACE: Temporal Audit and Condition-aware Evaluation of Streaming Video Understanding
entry.summary:
TRACE is a condition-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for streaming video understanding that audits evidence timing, history processing, and trigger annotations across 1,240 records from 517 videos.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to evaluate streaming video models as execution-conditioned systems, exposing critical performance operational trade-offs like latency and false alarms that standard accuracy metrics mask.

entry.title: ZooWork-ShopRanker: An Open, Preference-Aligned E-Commerce Reranker
entry.summary:
ZooWork-ShopRanker is an open e-commerce reranker family (0.6B, 4B, 8B) trained on preference signals labeled by a panel of reasoning LLM judges.

Why it matters: It provides open, specialized reranking models and evaluation benchmarks that bridge the performance gap between general web retrieval and preference-driven e-commerce search.

entry.title: Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching
entry.summary:
Continuous Depth Batching (CDB) enables efficient depth-adaptive inference in looped language models by dynamically re-batching tokens between loop steps and pre-building batches asynchronously based on exit predictions.

Why it matters: CDB removes the primary batching infrastructure bottleneck for depth-adaptive inference, allowing looped language models to translate theoretical token-level compute savings into real-world throughput gains.

entry.title: Morphometric Imitation: From Morphology and Contact Aware Hand Retargeting to Sim-to-Real Visuomotor Policy
entry.summary:
Morphometric Imitation is a three-stage framework that transforms human hand-object interactions into zero-shot sim-to-real robot visuomotor policies using contact-aware retargeting and residual reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It enables scalable transfer of complex human hand-object interactions to diverse robotic hands with high real-world success without requiring real-world policy retraining.

entry.title: MOPD-Router: Rethinking Teacher Routing in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
MOPD-Router is a domain-label-free framework that performs token-level routing across multiple teacher models during on-policy distillation using a specialized metric called ExpertAlign.

Why it matters: It enables multi-teacher distillation on unlabeled datasets while capturing cross-domain complementary signals that static prompt-level routing misses.

entry.title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
entry.summary:
Self-supervised confidence fine-tuning on intermediate reasoning steps reduces generated tokens by up to 25% at matched accuracy without explicitly optimizing for length or using early-stopping mechanisms.

Why it matters: Reasoning efficiency can be achieved indirectly by training models on metacognitive signals like confidence, avoiding complex length-penalty reinforcement learning or runtime early-stopping interventions.

entry.title: ActKV: Efficient LLM Agents through Action-Guided KV Cache Management
entry.summary:
ActKV is the first KV cache compression framework for agentic LLMs that prioritizes action-critical memory using action-oriented eviction, confidence-driven budget allocation, and page-aware GPU execution.

Why it matters: ActKV drastically reduces the memory footprint of long-horizon LLM agents, enabling significantly higher serving throughput without compromising agent decision-making accuracy.

entry.title: Evaluating the accuracy of KV cache reuse techniques
entry.summary:
A new evaluation methodology and dataset generation tool, Boxoffice, address flaws in existing benchmarks that artificially inflate the reported accuracy of position-independent KV cache reuse techniques.

Why it matters: Accurately measuring performance loss prevents the deployment of flawed KV cache reuse techniques that compromise generation accuracy in retrieval-augmented generation systems.

entry.title: Compact Documentation for Coding Agents: A Benchmark, an Optimizer, and Why It Does Not Transfer
entry.summary:
Researchers created a roundtrip benchmark and optimizer for generating complete code documentation, but discovered that adding static or retrieved documentation fails to improve coding agents' ability to resolve repository issues over using the issue text alone.

Why it matters: The negative result demonstrates that providing extra static or retrieved documentation to coding agents with access to source code does not improve real-world issue resolution performance.

entry.title: Multi-agent Scaling Across Disjunctive and Compensatory Tasks
entry.summary:
A study applies Steiner's task taxonomy to multi-agent LLM scaling, showing that plurality voting fails on disjunctive tasks and shared item-level biases prevent scaling gains on compensatory tasks like Fermi estimation.

Why it matters: Increasing LLM agent team sizes yields diminishing returns due to shared model biases and output aggregation limits, showing that task structure dictates multi-agent architecture success.

entry.title: Compress What You See, Not What You Say: Anchored Context Distillation for Latent-Observation Software Engineering Agents
entry.summary:
A framework combining Latent Observations, Hard Actions (LOHA) and Anchored Context Distillation (ACD) compresses older tool observations into soft tokens while preserving agent text actions, reducing context length and boosting execution throughput.

Why it matters: This method significantly cuts inference context costs and increases agent throughput without replacing critical exact-reference text or causing severe performance degradation.

entry.title: Highlight-Then-Summarize: Learning to Compress Evidence for Long-Context Understanding
entry.summary:
Highlight-Then-Summarize (H2S) is a compress-then-reason paradigm that identifies question-relevant evidence and integrates it into a compact summary before generating final answers for long-context reasoning tasks.

Why it matters: Explicitly highlighting and summarizing key evidence enables smaller language models to achieve superior long-context reasoning performance while using significantly fewer output tokens.

entry.title: Softmax Reparameterization for Output-Head Quantization
entry.summary:
Softmax reparameterization optimizes output-head quantization by subtracting a validation-selected scalar multiple of the vocabulary-row mean, preserving full-precision softmax distributions without changing the trained decoder.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces output-head quantization error and generation latency in small language models without requiring retraining or adding runtime compute overhead.

entry.title: MoSAR: Mixture of Semantic Attention Regimes for Learning Adaptive and Approximable Attention Geometries
entry.summary:
MoSAR introduces a Mixture of Semantic Attention Regimes that uses input-conditioned query and key routers to learn a continuous, distance-dependent attention field over short, medium, and global regimes.

Why it matters: It enables long-context language models to dynamically adjust attention reach based on input semantics without sacrificing perplexity or relying on predefined fixed sparsity patterns.

entry.title: Acoustic-to-Text KV Compression for Full-Duplex Speech Models
entry.summary:
Acoustic-to-text KV compression utilizes listening-time slack to convert incoming speech into compact textual memory, enabling 64.6% peak streaming KV-cache reduction during long-running full-duplex speech interactions.

Why it matters: It enables long-duration, memory-efficient full-duplex speech interaction on memory-constrained devices without sacrificing real-time conversational capabilities.

entry.title: How does Adversarial Influence Scale in Multi-Agent Systems?
entry.summary:
A study on multi-agent LLM deliberation shows that agent defection rates rise linearly with the proportion of deceivers, with LLMs succumbing to deceptive minorities unlike humans.

Why it matters: Simply scaling group size does not protect multi-agent LLM systems against adversarial subversion, as adversaries only need to maintain their proportion within the group.

entry.title: GHOST-Q: Towards Studying Grounding Hallucinations Overlooked Under Same-score TradeOffs in Quantized VLMS
entry.summary:
GHOST-Q evaluates 8B vision-language models across FP16, INT8, and NF4 precisions, revealing significant grounding hallucinations and generation budget censoring despite quantized variants maintaining baseline accuracy scores.

Why it matters: Evaluating quantized VLMs solely on aggregate accuracy scores risks masking critical visual grounding failures, hallucination risks, and unexpected latency bottlenecks in production deployments.

entry.title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
TRACE is an amortized temporal gradient-inversion attack that autoregressively reconstructs private observation-action trajectories from policy gradients in distributed embodied reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: Standard gradient-sharing mechanisms in embodied RL fail to protect sensor data, indicating that future privacy defenses must be sequence-aware to prevent trajectory leakage.

entry.title: Beyond Compression: Training Latent Representations for Stable Long-Horizon Rollout in Neural Surrogate Solvers
entry.summary:
A latent dynamics framework aligns autoencoders for long-horizon stability using Koopman learning, noise injection, and multi-step fine-tuning, reducing rollout error by 40% over standard reconstruction-only models.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that latent representations must be engineered specifically for temporal dynamics rather than pure spatial compression to build stable, computationally efficient neural surrogate solvers.

entry.title: Aim Short to Reach Far: Your Frozen World Model Can Plan Better Than You Think
entry.summary:
Anchored Planning improves visual world model control by directing a frozen LeWM model toward short-horizon intermediate targets retrieved from past experience rather than scoring directly against the distant final goal image.

Why it matters: Visual world models can solve complex, long-horizon tasks without costly retraining by simply altering the planning target to short-term intermediate goals.

entry.title: Let Training Guide Selection: Online Synthetic Data Filtering via Real-Anchored Utility
entry.summary:
FROST is an online framework that dynamically filters synthetic data using gradient feedback anchored in real training data, eliminating the need for external verifiers or held-out validation sets.

Why it matters: It enables models to selectively discard unhelpful or noisy synthetic samples on the fly, improving performance without requiring expensive manual annotations, external verifiers, or separate validation sets.

entry.title: CORDIAL: Calibrating Ordinal LLM Outputs from Few Labels
entry.summary:
CORDIAL calibrates ordinal LLM output distributions using a five-parameter channel that preserves first-order stochastic order and requires only a handful of labeled examples to infer its posterior.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the amount of labeled data required to calibrate LLM probability outputs on ordinal tasks, matching complex baselines with less than half the training labels.

entry.title: JevOut: Natural Context Can Flip Decision Models
entry.summary:
Researchers show that short, natural context additions can flip correct choices in dedicated decision models like Jev to high-confidence wrong options without changing the gold answer.

Why it matters: This extreme sensitivity to surrounding context highlights the risks of using language-based decision model probability outputs as reliable interfaces for automated downstream routing and action execution.

entry.title: Multimodal Thinking with Renderable Programs
entry.summary:
SVGLM enables vision-language models to incorporate images into their reasoning chains by generating renderable, scalable vector graphics (SVG) text primitives during the thought process.

Why it matters: SVG primitives offer a tractable, text-compatible medium for digital agents to perform visual reasoning without relying on complex pixel-level or latent generation.

entry.title: MILO: Efficient Many-shot In-Context Learning with Block-wise Low-rank Compression
entry.summary:
MILO is a context compression framework that applies block-wise low-rank KV cache compression and entropy-based dynamic rank allocation for efficient many-shot in-context learning.

Why it matters: MILO significantly reduces memory overhead and boosts throughput for long-context LLM inference, facilitating scalable online serving and on-device deployment.

entry.title: TimeBraid: Unifying Time Series and Language for Understanding and Forecasting
entry.summary:
TimeBraid is a model family that unifies pretrained language and time-series foundation models into a shared representation space using interleaved global residual attention layers for joint understanding and forecasting.

Why it matters: It enables a single unified architecture to perform time-series forecasting, temporal reasoning, and natural language instruction following without relying on task-specific models.

entry.title: C3M: Cross-Session Multimodal Memory Maintenance for Long-Horizon Tasks
entry.summary:
C3M is a cross-session multimodal memory architecture that maintains a bounded active index over persistent text-image evidence using relation-aware updates and budgeted query-time routing.

Why it matters: It enables long-horizon AI agents to retain precise visual and textual evidence across multiple sessions without exceeding fixed memory limits or discarding critical fine-grained details.

entry.title: IterSynth: Rethinking Deep Search Agents via Role-Decoupled Iterative Synthesis
entry.summary:
IterSynth replaces ReAct with a role-decoupled search framework that alternates between a Planner and a Synthesizer using an evolving summary state to reduce context noise.

Why it matters: IterSynth improves LLM search agent accuracy and efficiency by decoupling planning from synthesis and preventing performance degradation caused by bloated context windows.

entry.title: Rufus-Air: An Open LLM Post-Training Recipe
entry.summary:
Rufus-Air introduces an open, eight-stage post-training recipe for GLM-4.5-Air-Base (106B-A12B) that relies entirely on open-source components, public data, and verifiable-to-soft reward ordering without new human annotations.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive post-training performance on large mixture-of-experts models can be fully reproduced using public data and open-source infrastructure without human labels.

entry.title: Controlling Backchannels in Streamable Full-duplex Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced a lightweight backchannel head that uses hidden states from full-duplex spoken dialogue models to predict and force-decode backchannel timing via a tunable threshold.

Why it matters: It enables precise control over natural, real-time conversational acknowledgements in spoken dialogue systems without requiring complex model redesigns.

entry.title: Baseline Shape Decides the Verdict: A Controlled Re-Examination of Ternary Language Models at 60K Parameters
entry.summary:
A 98-run replication at 60K parameters shows that reported advantages of routed ternary models over transformers stem from suboptimal baseline depth/width shapes rather than inductive bias, with plain gated diagonal-SSMs actually outperforming routed architectures.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that sub-1M parameter model evaluations are highly sensitive to shape selection and hyperparameter tuning, preventing false attributions of performance gains to specialized routing mechanisms.

entry.title: Likelihood Ranking doesn't Scale Like Prompting in LLMs
entry.summary:
Across 95 decoder-only models, accuracy from likelihood ranking of declarative statements remains stable with model scale, whereas prompted answer accuracy improves sharply with scale and instruction-tuning.

Why it matters: Evaluators cannot treat declarative statement likelihood preferences and task-conditioned prompting as interchangeable metrics, as they measure distinct aspects of LLM behavior.

entry.title: Parts-of-Speech as Emergent Categories in SAE Latent Space
entry.summary:
A study reveals Sparse AutoEncoders localize part-of-speech categories in language models as compact, distributed groups of sparse latents rather than one-to-one feature mappings.

Why it matters: Understanding that SAEs represent grammar via distributed latent groups rather than single features helps researchers build better interpretability models for neural network representations.

entry.title: Rolling-WAM: World Action Models with Rolling Imagination
entry.summary:
Rolling-WAM accelerates robotic visual-action world models by distributing joint video-action denoising across successive replanning cycles using a sliding window and rolling noise schedule.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces action generation latency in World Action Models, enabling faster closed-loop control for real-time robotic manipulation.

entry.title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced VeriSpeak, a benchmark of 3,879 spoken claims, revealing that Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) struggle with a text-speech modality gap and require retrieval paired with explicit reasoning to effectively fact-check speech.

Why it matters: Detecting audio misinformation requires LALMs to go beyond speech recognition and integrate structured, grounded reasoning over retrieved textual evidence.

entry.title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records
entry.summary:
Researchers developed and clinician-validated an automated framework that generates the Benchmark for Retrieving Information in EHRs (BRIE), a continuously maintainable evaluation dataset derived from longitudinal EHR notes.

Why it matters: Automated, validated benchmark generation enables continuous, leakage-proof evaluation of clinical LLMs on complex patient record retrieval tasks without relying on static datasets.

entry.title: Does a model's stated reason for rejecting a candidate do any work?
entry.summary:
Inserting a model's stated missing fact into a rejected candidate profile significantly increases its selection odds over an irrelevant sentence control under greedy decoding, demonstrating that self-generated explanations reflect actionable decision drivers.

Why it matters: This research shows that LLM explanations for candidate rejections are not purely hallucinatory and correspond to real, leverageable features driving model selection logic.

entry.title: GRASP: Generating, Revising, and Assessing for Strategic Planning with Agentic AI
entry.summary:
GRASP is a strategy-aware, multi-stage planning framework that decouples task planning across context-isolated modules to generate high-quality natural language executable plans for complex tasks.

Why it matters: By preventing performance collapse during complex, multi-task scaling, GRASP enables LLMs to execute highly intricate, multi-step natural language plans reliably.

entry.title: EnigmaForge: The Question Is Hidden in the Story
entry.summary:
EnigmaForge is a novel benchmark that hides SAT-verified logic puzzles inside generated narrative documents without explicitly providing the target question to the model.

Why it matters: It exposes critical gaps in model reasoning and task discovery that standard direct-question benchmarks fail to measure, while avoiding dataset contamination via infinite procedural generation.

entry.title: HEXIS: Compiling Skills into Extended Finite State Machines
entry.summary:
HEXIS compiles agent skills into extended finite state machines (EFSMs), decoupling control flow from task reasoning to enforce execution structure and reduce LLM generation overhead.

Why it matters: By enforcing deterministic control flow via state machines, agents reliably follow prescribed multi-step procedures while significantly cutting LLM token costs.
